title: Title Accounting Calculation Note: Title & Registration Services Fee-Shortage Cure Payment
content:
When the state sends a Title & Registration Services packet back for a fee shortage, the buyer's cure payment is the shortage the state stated on the order's most recent fee-shortage return, collected from the buyer as its own fee entry booked against the registration fee. The payment is rounded half up to the cent, only once and at the end of the calculation.

## Where the figure comes from

| Quantity | Record |
|---|---|
| the order's most recent fee-shortage return | among the state rejection entries on the title order whose reason is fee shortage, the one with the latest date |
| the stated shortage | the amount the state stated on that return |
| booking of the cure payment | a fee entry of its own on the title order, under the registration fee |

An earlier fee-shortage return on the same order does not enter the payment: only the most recent one is read.

## Worked example (hypothetical order)

The title order shows two state rejection entries for fee shortage: one dated 4 April stating 18.00 and one dated 9 May stating 46.35.

1. The most recent fee-shortage return is the one dated 9 May.
2. Its stated shortage is 46.35.
3. The buyer's cure payment is 46.35, already a whole number of cents, booked as its own entry against the registration fee.

## Second worked example (hypothetical order)

A single fee-shortage return states 27.80. The buyer's cure payment is 27.80.
